Here's a regex for an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is a four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is a month from 01 to 12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is a day from 01 to 31.
- `^…$` anchors the match to the whole string. To find dates inside longer text, swap the anchors for `\b`.

It matches `2026-10-01` and rejects `2026-13-01` and `2026-10-32`.

It doesn't check that the day exists in that month, so `2026-02-31` still matches. Regex can't handle that well, so validate those cases with a date parser. A leap-year-aware regex is possible but long.
